duration.text: The Food science and technology at Jiangnan University is a 3 Years long program for international students, taught in English.

fees.text: Application Fee: $ 150 USD Service Fee: $ 50 USD Tuition fee: $ 2777 USD/per year ￥ 20000 CNY/per year

materials.text: Color scan copies of the passport (including the photo page and the visa page) Photographs taken within the last 6 months (no headwear, frontal vertical format, 1-inch ID photo, JPG or JPEG format, not exceeding 1MB) Color scanned copy of the undergraduate graduation certificate (Fresh graduates can provide a pre-graduation certificate first) Color scanned copies of all course transcripts from the undergraduate period Color scanned copy of the official score report from the Chinese/English proficiency test (original certificate must be provided during registration for verification) Guide's Acceptance Letter from Jiangnan University (see the attached file below) Research Plan Two recommendation letters Economic guarantee certificate (see the attached document below) Deposit certificate (bank transaction record proof within the past 6 months) Certificate of No Criminal Record Physical examination report (within 6 months) (see the attached file below) To apply for the design major, at least 3 pieces of work must be submitted.

requirements.text: 1. The applicant must be a non-Chinese citizen and in good health. 2. Requirements for applicant's education and age: Those who come to China to pursue a master's degree must have completed their undergraduate studies before enrollment, and their age should not exceed 40 years old. 3. Language Requirements: Applicants for Chinese-taught programs must have a HSK 4 certificate or above. For applicants majoring in Chinese and history-related fields, they must have a HSK 5 certificate or above. (2) Applicants for programs taught entirely in English must have an IELTS score of 6.0 or above, a TOEFL score of 80 or above, or a CEFR B2 (European Common Reference Framework) certificate or other proof of English proficiency. For pre-requisite courses taught entirely in English, no English proficiency certificate is required.
